title: Sorting and Filtering Data in SQLite with DB Browser
description: A beginner-friendly course that teaches how to explore, sort, and filter data in an e-commerce orders table using DB Browser for SQLite, building skills step by step without writing any SQL.
target_audience: Beginner data analysts with no SQL experience

videos.title: Browsing Your First Table
videos.learning_objective: Understand how data is organized into rows and columns within a table.
videos.discovery_objective: Open the Orders table in the Browse Data tab and display all rows with columns order_id, customer_name, order_date, amount, and status visible.

exercise_artifact.description: A single table of customer orders used consistently across all videos to teach sorting and filtering.

videos.new_capability: Opening and viewing a table's full contents in Browse Data tab
videos.running_example_usage: The learner opens the Orders table to see every order record before any sorting or filtering.
videos.proof_numbers: The Orders table contains 120 rows and 5 columns.
videos.preview_text_hint: Next we'll sort the Orders table by amount to see the smallest orders first.

videos.title: Sorting a Column in Ascending Order
videos.learning_objective: Understand how clicking a column header arranges rows from smallest to largest value.
videos.discovery_objective: In the Browse Data tab, click the amount column header of the Orders table so rows display in ascending order.

exercise_artifact.description: A single table of customer orders used consistently across all videos to teach sorting and filtering.

videos.new_capability: Sorting a single column in ascending order by clicking its header
videos.running_example_usage: The learner sorts the Orders table by amount to find the cheapest orders first.
videos.proof_numbers: After sorting ascending, the smallest amount value appears at the top of 120 rows.
videos.recap_text_hint: In the last video we opened the Orders table and saw all 120 rows with order_id, customer_name, order_date, amount, and status columns.
videos.preview_text_hint: Next we'll click the same column header again to reverse the sort order and find the largest orders.

videos.title: Reversing the Sort Order
videos.learning_objective: Understand how clicking a sorted column header again reverses the order from largest to smallest.
videos.discovery_objective: In the Browse Data tab, click the amount column header of the Orders table a second time so rows display in descending order.

exercise_artifact.description: A single table of customer orders used consistently across all videos to teach sorting and filtering.

videos.new_capability: Toggling a column sort from ascending to descending order
videos.running_example_usage: The learner reverses the amount sort on the Orders table to see the highest-value orders first.
videos.proof_numbers: After sorting descending, the largest amount value appears at the top of 120 rows.
videos.recap_text_hint: In the last video we sorted the Orders table by amount in ascending order, placing the smallest amount at the top.
videos.preview_text_hint: Next we'll filter the Orders table to show only rows with a specific status value.

videos.title: Filtering Rows by a Single Condition
videos.learning_objective: Understand how typing a value into a column filter box narrows the visible rows to matching records.
videos.discovery_objective: In the Browse Data tab, type Shipped into the status column filter box of the Orders table so only matching rows are displayed.

exercise_artifact.description: A single table of customer orders used consistently across all videos to teach sorting and filtering.

videos.new_capability: Filtering a table by entering a value in a single column's filter box
videos.running_example_usage: The learner filters the Orders table to isolate only orders with a status of Shipped.
videos.proof_numbers: Filtering status equal to Shipped reduces the visible rows from 120 to 46.
videos.recap_text_hint: In the last video we reversed the sort on the Orders table so the highest amount appeared first among 120 rows.

running_example.name: E-commerce Orders
running_example.description: A single table of customer orders used consistently across all videos to teach sorting and filtering.
